edges.scope: spend control process
edges.evidence: Service Manual (updated 2026-04-01): "Digital and technology spend controls were replaced on 1 April 2026. From this date, central government departments are responsible for making most of their own digital and technology spending decisions." TCoP (updated 2025-07-07) still says: "You must consider all points of the TCoP as part of the Cabinet Office spend control process."
edges.guidance: Treat the Service Manual as current on who approves digital spend. TCoP remains current on the technology standards themselves, only its spend control section is stale.

edges.scope: digital service assessment and spend approval thresholds
edges.evidence: The agile business case clarification (2024-08-28) refers to CDDO-led assessments and the pre-2026 spend control thresholds.
edges.guidance: Check current thresholds in the Service Manual before relying on the £10m figure.

edges.scope: appraisal to evaluation
edges.evidence: The Green Book covers appraisal (before) and the Magenta Book covers evaluation (during and after). They are two halves of the same ROAMEF cycle.

edges.guidance: No public replacement. Current material sits on the OneFinance intranet.

edges.scope: evaluation findings inform future appraisal
delivery confidence assessment of the major projects portfolio
programme business case approval points
edges.evidence: Business case guidance (2026), 5.8: "There is only a single Gate for PBCs, which is Gate Review 0." 5.10: "Practitioners should undertake a Gate 0 Review when the PBC is first completed, ahead of the first approval point for the programme."

edges.scope: Outline Business Case (OBC) approval
edges.evidence: Business case guidance (2026), Table 2: "Gate 2: Delivery Strategy. Prior to Outline Business Case (OBC) approval." Gate 2 workbook: "Confirm the Outline Business Case (OBC) now the project is fully defined".

edges.scope: an approved Full Business Case before going live
edges.evidence: Gate 4 workbook, evidence expected: "The Project and HMT have been in dialogue about the full business case and HMT and both the Department Finance Director and HMT have signed off the FBC."

edges.scope: an approved evaluation plan
edges.evidence: Gate 4 workbook, project documentation: "A Magenta Book compliant Evaluation Plan approved by the Department Investment Committee and HMT if appropriate."

edges.scope: designing and running services
edges.evidence: GovS 005 v2.2, 5.3: "Services shall be delivered in accordance with the Service Standard."

edges.scope: expectations for technology decisions
edges.evidence: GovS 005 v2.2, 1.3: "This standard is supported by The Service Standard, which sets expectations for services, and the Technology Code of Practice, which sets expectations for technology decisions."

edges.scope: technology design and data sharing in DDaT procurement
edges.evidence: DDaT Playbook (2023), Key policies: data should be shared using APIs which "satisfy the requirements of the Technology Code of Practice (TCoP)". Governance and approvals: "TCoP is a cross-government standard setting out the key considerations for how the government should design, build and buy technology."

edges.scope: service assessments for DDaT services
edges.evidence: DDaT Playbook (2023), DDaT assurance: "services will also need to meet the Government Service Standard".

edges.scope: sourcing and contracting for digital, data and technology
edges.evidence: DDaT Playbook: "The Digital, Data and Technology Playbook is part of a wider portfolio of Sourcing Playbooks developed by the Cabinet Office." Sourcing Playbook: "The DDaT Playbook provides guidance when sourcing and contracting for these digital services."

edges.scope: sourcing consultancy services
edges.evidence: Consultancy Playbook v1.1, Scope: "The Consultancy Playbook forms part of the Sourcing Playbook. As such, the principles, guidelines and rules of the Sourcing Playbook still apply and shall be considered alongside the Consultancy Playbook where appropriate."

edges.scope: Integrated Assurance and Approval Plans submitted for Treasury approval
edges.evidence: Integrated assurance guide v2.1: the initial IAAP should be "validated by NISTA and HM Treasury, in sufficient time for appropriate planned assurance to take place prior to submission of a Strategic Outline Business Case (SOBC) to HM Treasury for approval." "The process for submission of IAAPs is described in the Treasury Approvals Process for projects and programmes".

edges.scope: who assures TCoP compliance and approves digital and technology spend
edges.evidence: DDaT Playbook (2023), DDaT assurance: "Compliance with this code is assured through the Cabinet Office spend control process". Service Manual (updated 2026-04-01): "Digital and technology spend controls were replaced on 1 April 2026."
edges.guidance: Treat the Service Manual as current on who approves digital and technology spend. The rest of the playbook, including its separate commercial spend control, is not affected by this.

edges.scope: technology spend control sign-off before going live
edges.evidence: Gate 4 workbook (republished 2026-08-20), 4.2: "Cabinet Office (CO) controls have been sighted on the FBC and the project has satisfied the CO controls teams commercial and technology spend control requirements." Service Manual (updated 2026-04-01): "Digital and technology spend controls were replaced on 1 April 2026."
edges.guidance: The two disagree on technology spend control; this library cannot say which is right. Check with NISTA or the department's digital spend approvers. The commercial spend control in the same sentence is a separate control.

edges.scope: benefits evidence at the strategic assessment
edges.evidence: Benefits assurance guide v2.1, Gate 0: "Benefits slogan: 'Link benefits to strategy'... Key question: 'Are the project benefits contributing to the wider strategic objectives of the programme / department / HMG?'"

edges.scope: benefits evidence at business justification
edges.evidence: Benefits assurance guide v2.1, Gate 1: "Benefits slogan: 'Identify benefits'", followed by the key question and the benefits documents required at that gate.

edges.scope: benefits evidence at delivery strategy
edges.evidence: Benefits assurance guide v2.1, Gate 2: "Benefits slogan: 'Value and appraise'... For an Outline Business Case a selection of the most important benefits identified will need to be valued".

edges.scope: benefits evidence at the investment decision
edges.evidence: Benefits assurance guide v2.1, Gate 3: "Benefits slogan: 'Plan to realise'", followed by the key question and the benefits documents required at that gate.

edges.scope: benefits evidence at readiness for service
edges.evidence: Benefits assurance guide v2.1, Gate 4: "Benefits slogan: 'Work to realise'... Key question: 'are the correct processes in place to ensure benefits continue to be realised after the project transitions into business as usual?'"

edges.scope: benefits evidence at the operations review
edges.evidence: Benefits assurance guide v2.1, Gate 5: "Benefits slogan: 'Review performance'", followed by the key question and the benefits documents required at that gate.

edges.scope: planning assurance and approvals (the IAAP)
edges.evidence: Business case guidance (2026), 11.10: "Practitioners should develop an integrated assurance and approval plan (IAAP)."

edges.scope: appropriate and responsible use of data and AI
edges.evidence: GovS 005 v2.2, 7.2: organisations "should use the Data and AI Ethics Framework to ensure data and AI are used appropriately, responsibly and transparently".

edges.scope: creating a secure service (Service Standard point 9)
edges.evidence: Secure by Design, About (security.gov.uk, read 2026-10-15): "The Service Standard Point 9 (Create a secure service which protects users' privacy) advises service teams that they must follow the Secure by Design principles."

edges.scope: producing quality analysis
edges.evidence: Magenta Book, 4.4 Data quality: "The Aqua Book and the Green Book provide further guidance on producing quality analysis for government."

edges.scope: managing knowledge assets
edges.evidence: Rose Book (2024): "This guidance is to advise and support organisations in scope with their knowledge asset management and, in turn, fulfil their responsibilities as set out in Managing Public Money (MPM)."

edges.scope: knowledge asset management in projects
edges.evidence: Teal Book, 24.4 What is information and data management?: "The Rose Book: Knowledge asset management in government provides further guidance on this."

edges.scope: algorithmic transparency, for departments and in-scope arm's-length bodies
edges.evidence: AI Playbook, Principle 7: "If you're a central government department or an arm's length body within scope, you're required to use the Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard (ATRS)."

edges.scope: algorithmic transparency, for departments and in-scope arm's-length bodies
edges.evidence: Data and AI Ethics Framework, Using the Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard: "All central government departments and arm's length bodies that provide public or frontline services, or routinely interact with the general public, must use the ATRS."

edges.scope: assessing an organisation's adherence to the standard
edges.evidence: GovS 002 CIAF v2.1: "This assessment framework is designed to help drive continuous improvement within and across government, by helping government organisations assess their adherence to, and practical application of the project delivery functional standard".

edges.scope: algorithmic transparency
edges.evidence: GovS 005 v2.2, 7.1: "Organisations should follow cross-government strategies, standards and governance for government digital and data, including ... the Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard, and relevant security, privacy and technology standards".

edges.scope: identifying, protecting and exploiting knowledge assets
edges.evidence: Green Book, Assets: "The Rose Book provides guidance on how to identify, protect and exploit knowledge assets."

edges.scope: standards for analysis and data use within project delivery
edges.evidence: Teal Book, 24.6.1.4: "the Government Functional Standard for Analysis and the Aqua Book (requires sign in) set out standards for data use in analysis, and these should be followed where such activities are part of the scope of the work."
